text: Understanding Git branching is essential for modern software development. A branch lets you work on new features without affecting the main codebase. Developers create feature branches to add new functionality or fix bugs safely. Once the work is complete, they merge the branch back into the main project. Teams often use pull requests to review changes before merging, which improves code quality and encourages collaboration. This version control workflow keeps projects organized and reduces conflicts between developers. By using branches, pull requests, and merging effectively, teams can work together smoothly and deliver better software faster.
